questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that I chose a city where I could improve my English languae by choosing English subjects as well as meeting new people. Milan is a very international city and I have always loved the Italian culture which made my choice of going to Milan very easy. Also, I wanted to stay wihtin Europe to be able to choose subejcts af the receiving institution within European Law, which I did at my semester abroad in Milan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I rate mit stay in Milan with an 8 out of 10 as my stay overall was super good. The only thing that i would do differently is that I would live with other international students or some locals if I could do something differently as I then would improve my English even better and get to know other cultures more.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy as most information was either on the receiving institution's website or provided to me by email which made it easy to know, what I needed to do upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance when I arrived at my study destination. I did not need any or ask for any either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing via Airbnb. I did not know anything about where I could find housing outside of Airbnb. It was very expensive so I would have liked some more information with this regard.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there are several websites where you can find accommodation, but I think it would be useful for future exchange students to get some more information about this topic.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At the hos institutions website for students, we were able to register for all of their courses online. It was very easy and we could change it when we needed without any issued.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not get any help on this. If any, I asked my teacher about the website and she explained how I needed to register.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the classes i prefered and wanted without problems apart from one as the teacher got sick and couldn't host the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask your teacher about the registering, they are very nice and want to help you. Otherwise, they should be provided with a detailed guide on this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was not as high as the ones here in Denmark. But the most important for me was to improve my English language which I managed to do.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. The teachers did not interact with the students as much as they do here in Denmark. Also, we had a lot of influence on the exams (which kind of exam we wanted) which is very different from UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Law and policies on Social rights protection in Europe
Public and private partnership for sustainable development
Smart cities, artificial intelligence and digital transformation law
Access to justice in a multilevel constitutional system
Comparative labour law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. the teacher were super good and nice, the level of English was acceptable and the exams were good and suitable. I would recommend all of the courses to future exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than I expected. I had a situation where my originally planned housing was cancelled 2 weeks before my exchange period began, so I think that my housing got more expensive as I was out too late.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure, as I didn't attend any of such activities at the host institution. We mostly attended events outside of the institution, for example Erasmus events at clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend other students to attend Erasmus events as this was a great way of meeting other international students at a more chill setting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: They should experience walking on the roof of the cathedral in Milan as well as just walking around in the streets of Navigli and by the Duomo. Otherwise I would recommend them to explore the restuarants as there are many good places to eat.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The culture is not much different from the Danish culture and the milanese people were very friendly and open. The most challenging was the language barrier as some italian people were not super well at the english language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As mentioned in the above, the only difficult aspect was the language as some italians were not super good in english. Although, they tried and we found a way to communicate with our hands and expressions.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The part of the culture I appreciated the most was that we went out to eat a lot and got "apperitivo" after classes which is a classic italian way of gathering before dinner to get drinks and snacks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. To make sure always to be with someone else at night to be safe and feel safe
2. Make sure to attend to as many social events as possible from the beginning to build a social network 
3. Attend to classes and be active in the classes as this will make your study and exam period much more exiting and giving.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I have written down all the useful information I had in the above answers

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friendships and my improvement of the english language

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Standing on my own feet in a foreign country, but this is both challenging but also very giving and I learned a lot about myself and the world.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
